chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He who humiliates a believer and belittles him due to the scarcity of his wealth and for his poverty, Allah will publicize him on the Day of Judgment upon the heads of the creatures.

key_terms.ذَاتِ يَدِهِ: Wealth or means (literally: what is in the hand)
key_terms.رُءُوسِ الْخَلَائِقِ: Heads of the creatures (publicly before all)
key_terms.شَهَرَهُ: To publicize or expose (often with disgrace)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of humiliating a poor believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing that despising a believer for material poverty is a grave ethical breach that invites divine humiliation. This 'shahara' (public exposure) serves as a cosmic reversal of status, reminding the faithful that true worth lies in piety rather than wealth, a core tenet of Shia moral theology.
